evidence: Objective 1 (identify types of plane shapes and their properties, similarities and differences) is addressed in full, with comparison tables for triangles, square/rectangle, and parallelogram/trapezium.
Objective 2 (identify parts of a circle) is covered completely: arc, radius, chord, diameter, circumference, segment, sector, and tangent are all named and explained.

Objective 3 (find perimeter of regular polygon, square, rectangle, trapezium, parallelogram and circle) is addressed with formulas and nine worked examples, including reverse problems (finding missing side or radius).
objective_curriculum_alignment.rationale: All three lesson objectives are addressed thoroughly and in the order stated, with the level of coverage matching a JSS1 third-term curriculum target on plane shapes and perimeter. Nothing from the objectives appears to have been omitted.

evidence: The teacher's lesson sequence (shapes and properties → parts of a circle → perimeter) is preserved exactly in the three sections of the revision pack.

The teacher's evaluation questions are reproduced almost verbatim in the practice section (e.g., perimeter of a square of 8 cm, rectangle 7 cm × 4 cm, regular pentagon 5 cm, parallelogram base 6 cm and side 5 cm, circumference 22 cm find radius, rectangle breadth d), showing close alignment with how the lesson was assessed.

One element from the lesson (the unlabelled composite figure marked 1 cm, 5 cm, 9 cm) does not appear in the pack; also, the pack adds a quarter-circle worked example and a polygon-naming table that go slightly beyond what the teacher explicitly presented.
taught_lesson_alignment.rationale: The pack mirrors the teacher's sequence and depth very faithfully, and nearly all teacher evaluation questions reappear as practice items. Minor gaps (the composite figure question) and slight additions (quarter-circle, extended polygon table) keep the score just below a perfect 5.

evidence: All perimeter formulas and worked-example calculations are arithmetically correct (e.g., circumference 22 cm giving r = 3.5 cm is verified correctly; hexagon 6 × 5.2 = 31.2 cm is correct).
The parts-of-a-circle definitions are accurate: diameter defined as a chord through the centre, tangent defined as touching at exactly one point, segment and sector correctly distinguished.

One figure description mentions 'A shape made from a quarter circle: two straight sides of 4.9 cm meeting at a right angle' — the cylinder-with-rope figure description that appears among the worked-example figures seems out of place and unrelated to the lesson content, suggesting an erroneous asset crept in; it does not affect the mathematics but slightly mars scope.
scope_conceptual_correctness.rationale: The mathematics and definitions throughout the pack are correct and well within JSS1 scope. The only blemish is an apparently stray figure description (the cylinder with a rope) that has no connection to the lesson and should not be there.

evidence: Each section follows a clear Explain → Worked Example(s) → Practice → Answers structure that allows a student working alone at home to study, attempt questions, and check their own work.

Language is plain and accessible: concepts are introduced with everyday analogies ('imagine running a pencil all the way around the circle') and step-by-step working is shown in full, with units carried through every calculation.

The comparison tables (triangle types, square vs rectangle, parallelogram vs trapezium) and the polygon-naming table give JSS1 learners a compact visual reference they can return to when answering the practice questions.
clarity_usefulness.rationale: The pack is exceptionally well-structured for independent home use: explanations are age-appropriate, worked examples model every question type that appears in the practice, and full answers allow self-assessment. A JSS1 student should be able to navigate it without a teacher present.
